calls.head: The Jets want Vilardi away from the big guns
calls.body: At home, the Jets keep sending Vilardi’s line (Niederreiter, Vilardi and Björck) out against opponents’ third lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Scott Arniel has been chasing an easier matchup for the team’s scorers. Tonight the Hurricanes’ third line is Jankowski, Martinook and Ehlers.

surprises.head: Both teams played to type
surprises.body: Nothing in this game strayed far from how these two usually play: the shot share, the quality of chances, special teams, hitting, ice time and goaltending all landed inside their normal night-to-night range.

story.head: The Hurricanes make it seven straight
paras: The second period was a wild one. Mark Scheifele opened the scoring for the Jets early in the period. Mark Jankowski tied it 1-1 for Carolina on the power play just under four minutes later, his sixth straight game with a goal. Alex Iafallo put the Jets up 2-1 less than three minutes later, but that’s where Winnipeg’s luck ran out. Jesperi Kotkaniemi tied it up for Carolina late in the second, and Nikolaj Ehlers put the Hurricanes ahead for good on the power play midway through the third.

The Hurricanes outshot the Jets 37-23, but the Jets’ looks were better, so the chances came out about even. Pyotr Kochetkov made 21 saves for the Hurricanes, and Clay Stevenson stopped 34 of 37. The Canes improved to 7-1-1, and the Jets dropped to 4-2-2.

items.text: The Hurricanes are rolling: seven straight wins.
Mark Scheifele has a point in five straight games.
The Hurricanes have beaten the Jets four straight times, going back to the 2024-25 season.
With Jordan Staal out, Jankowski took his spot and scored.
